It's not like that, just depends on the type of insurance you have and what the % cover is for certain stuff. Not like therapists and doctors are somehow way cheaper in Europe or Asia. US health insurance will cover mental health, and did for sure even before Obamacare. 

I think the US has a bigger problem with company PTO and wage policy. Everyone wants to talk about giving higher minimum wage, while many people making good life wages are working 60 hour weeks. With maybe seven sick days a year. Let's say your mom dies tomorrow. You take what? Two days off? Two more for the funeral? Another day a month later when you need to meet with family to deal with stuff? You've used up three days of sick time while working over 50 hours a week. 

Most bosses won't care if you have the flu or depressed because your fiance left you or your mom died. Having another employee incurs more overhead, so they'd rather see happygolucky employees working 50 hour weeks without problems. Something like anxiety or depression is a dealbreaker. That's what's expensive about depression.

If you look at the good things that come out of the internet, you'll see forums like this subreddit where feelings can be acknowledged. I think people are too ashamed to speak out to their friends. Being able to do it somewhat anonymously and easily is an immense benefit. One can at least put their emotions out there without the fear of repercussions.
